text:
**I’d pick the First Direct 1st Account debit card** if you’re opening a UK account for travel. There’s no monthly account fee, and First Direct passes on the Mastercard exchange rate without adding a fee for purchases abroad. You can also withdraw up to £500 a day in local currency without a First Direct fee, though the cash machine operator may charge its own. ([firstdirect.com](https://www.firstdirect.com/banking/travel-debit-card/))

If you already have a **Starling debit card**, I’d use that rather than open another account just for the trip. It also gives you fee-free purchases at the Mastercard rate; the main difference is a lower cash withdrawal limit of £300 a day. ([starlingbank.com](https://www.starlingbank.com/travel/?utm_source=openai))

**At the till or cash machine, choose the local currency, not GBP.** That way you get the card’s exchange rate rather than the merchant’s or cash machine’s, which is usually worse. ([firstdirect.com](https://www.firstdirect.com/banking/travel-debit-card/))
